literal: Because of those who possess noble character, the world exists; if that is not there, entering the earth, it would surely perish.
translation: The world continues to exist because it rests upon those who possess noble character; if not for them, it would sink into the dust and perish.
modern: நற்பண்பு உடையவர்களால் தான் இந்த உலகம் இயங்கிக் கொண்டிருக்கிறது; அது இல்லாவிட்டால், இவ்வுலகம் மண்ணுக்குள் புகுந்து அழிந்துபோகும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights how essential virtuous and courteous people are to the survival of human society. The word 'pattu' here means 'resting upon' or 'sustained by', indicating that the orderly existence of the world depends entirely on the presence of those with noble character. If such character ('atu') is absent, the poet warns that the world would 'pukku' (enter) the 'man' (earth/dust) and 'mayvatu' (perish). The emphatic particle 'man' underscores the absolute certainty of this social collapse and ruin in the absence of goodness.
